Tato [M 0.0038] paraṃ sarīre dvattiṃsadantaṭṭhikānaṃ visuṃ gahitattā sesāni catusaṭṭhi hatthaṭṭhikāni catusaṭṭhi pādaṭṭhikāni catusaṭṭhi mudukaṭṭhikāni maṃsanissitāni dve paṇhikaṭṭhīni ekekasmiṃ pāde dve dve gopphakaṭṭhikāni dve jaṅghaṭṭhikāni ekaṃ jaṇṇukaṭṭhi ekaṃ ūruṭṭhi dve kaṭiṭṭhīni aṭṭhārasa piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṭṭhīni catuvīsati phāsukaṭṭhīni cuddasa uraṭṭhīni ekaṃ hadayaṭṭhi dve akkhakaṭṭhīni dve piṭṭhibāhaṭṭhīni dve bāhaṭṭhīni dve dve aggabāhaṭṭhīni satta gīvaṭṭhīni dve hanukaṭṭhīni ekaṃ nāsikaṭṭhi dve akkhiṭṭhīni dve kaṇṇaṭṭhīni ekaṃ nalāṭaṭṭhi ekaṃ muddhaṭṭhi nava sīsakapālaṭṭhīnīti evamādinā nayena vuttappabhedāni aṭṭhīni sabbāneva vaṇṇato setānīti vavatthapeti.

After that, in the body, since the thirty-two teeth-bones are taken separately, there are the remaining bones: sixty-four hand-bones; sixty-four foot-bones; sixty-four soft-bones dependent on the flesh; two heel-bones; four ankle-bones, two in each foot; two shin-bones; one knee-bone; one thigh-bone; two hip-bones; eighteen spinal-vertebrae; twenty-four rib-bones; fourteen chest-bones; one heart-bone; two collarbones; two shoulder-blade-bones; two upper-arm-bones; four forearm-bones, two in each arm; seven neck-bones; two jaw-bones; one nose-bone; two eye-socket-bones; two ear-bones; one forehead-bone; one crown-bone; and nine skull-bones. In this way, one determines that all the bones whatsoever, described with their various distinctions, are white by way of color.

Saṇṭhānato nānāsaṇṭhānāni. Tathā hi tattha aggapādaṅguliyaṭṭhīni katakabījasaṇṭhānāni, tadanantarāni aṅgulīnaṃ majjhapabbaṭṭhīni aparipuṇṇapanasaṭṭhisaṇṭhānāni, mūlapabbaṭṭhīni paṇavasaṇṭhānāni, morasakalisaṇṭhānānītipi eke. Piṭṭhipādaṭṭhīni koṭṭitakandalakandarāsisaṇṭhānāni paṇhikaṭṭhīni ekaṭṭhitālaphalabījasaṇṭhānāni, gopphakaṭṭhīni ekatobaddhakīḷāgoḷakasaṇṭhānāni, jaṅghaṭṭhikesu khuddakaṃ dhanudaṇḍasaṇṭhānaṃ, mahantaṃ khuppipāsāmilātadhamanipiṭṭhisaṇṭhānaṃ, jaṅghaṭṭhikassa gopphakaṭṭhikesu patiṭṭhitaṭṭhānaṃ apanītatacakhajjūrīkaḷīrasaṇṭhānaṃ, jaṅghaṭṭhikassa jaṇṇukaṭṭhike patiṭṭhitaṭṭhānaṃ mudiṅgamatthakasaṇṭhānaṃ jaṇṇukaṭṭhi ekapassato ghaṭṭitapheṇasaṇṭhānaṃ, ūruṭṭhīni duttacchitavāsipharasudaṇḍasaṇṭhānāni, ūruṭṭhikassa kaṭaṭṭhike patiṭṭhitaṭṭhānaṃ suvaṇṇakārānaṃ aggijālanakasalākābundisaṇṭhānaṃ[P 0.0050], tappatiṭṭhitokāso aggacchinnapunnāgaphalasaṇṭhāno, kaṭiṭṭhīni dvepi ekābaddhāni hutvā kumbhakārehi katacullisaṇṭhānāni, tāpasabhisikāsaṇṭhānānītipi eke. Ānisadaṭṭhīni heṭṭhāmukhaṭhapitasappaphaṇasaṇṭhānāni, sattaṭṭhaṭṭhānesu chiddāvachiddāni aṭṭhārasa piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṭṭhīni abbhantarato uparūpari ṭhapitasīsakapaṭṭaveṭhakasaṇṭhānāni, bāhirato vaṭṭanāvalisaṇṭhānāni, tesaṃ antarantarā kakacadantasadisāni dve tīṇi kaṇṭakāni honti, catuvīsatiyā [M 0.0039] phāsukaṭṭhīsu paripuṇṇāni paripuṇṇasīhaḷadāttasaṇṭhānāni[V 0.0038], aparipuṇṇāni aparipuṇṇasīhaḷadāttasaṇṭhānāni, sabbāneva odātakukkuṭassa pasāritapakkhadvayasaṇṭhānānītipi eke. Cuddasa uraṭṭhīni jiṇṇasandamānikaphalakapantisaṇṭhānāni, hadayaṭṭhi dabbiphaṇasaṇṭhānaṃ, akkhakaṭṭhīni khuddakalohavāsidaṇḍasaṇṭhānāni, tesaṃ heṭṭhā aṭṭhi addhacandasaṇṭhānaṃ, piṭṭhibāhaṭṭhīni pharasuphaṇasaṇṭhānāni, upaḍḍhacchinnasīhaḷakudālasaṇṭhānānītipi eke. Bāhaṭṭhīni ādāsadaṇḍasaṇṭhānāni, mahāvāsidaṇḍasaṇṭhānānītipi eke. Aggabāhaṭṭhīni yamakatālakandasaṇṭhānāni, maṇibandhaṭṭhīni ekato alliyāpetvā ṭhapitasīsakapaṭṭaveṭhakasaṇṭhānāni, piṭṭhihatthaṭṭhīni koṭṭitakandalakandarāsisaṇṭhānāni, hatthaṅgulimūlapabbaṭṭhīni paṇavasaṇṭhānāni, majjhapabbaṭṭhīni aparipuṇṇapanasaṭṭhisaṇṭhānāni, aggapabbaṭṭhīni katakabījasaṇṭhānāni, satta gīvaṭṭhīni daṇḍe vijjhitvā paṭipāṭiyā ṭhapitavaṃsakaḷīrakhaṇḍasaṇṭhānāni, heṭṭhimahanukaṭṭhi kammārānaṃ ayokūṭayottakasaṇṭhānaṃ, uparimahanukaṭṭhi avalekhanasatthakasaṇṭhānaṃ, akkhināsakūpaṭṭhīni apanītamiñjataruṇatālaṭṭhisaṇṭhānāni[P 0.0051], nalāṭaṭṭhi adhomukhaṭhapitabhinnasaṅkhakapālasaṇṭhānaṃ, kaṇṇacūḷikaṭṭhīni nhāpitakhurakosasaṇṭhānāni, nalāṭakaṇṇacūḷikānaṃ upari paṭṭabandhanokāse aṭṭhibahalaghaṭapuṇṇapaṭapilotikakhaṇḍasaṇṭhānaṃ, muddhanaṭṭhi mukhacchinnavaṅkanāḷikerasaṇṭhānaṃ, sīsaṭṭhīni sibbetvā ṭhapitajajjarālābukaṭāhasaṇṭhānānīti. Disato dvīsu disāsu jātāni.

By way of shape, they are of various shapes. For indeed, among them, the bones of the tips of the toes are of the shape of a clearing-nut seed (kataka). Next to them, the middle joint bones of the toes are of the shape of an incomplete jackfruit seed. The base joint bones are of the shape of a paṇava drum; some also say they are of the shape of a peacock's neck joint. The bones of the dorsum of the foot are of the shape of a heap of tendons from a pounded kandala plant. The heel bone is of the shape of the seed of a single-seeded palmyra fruit. The ankle bones are of the shape of playing marbles bound together. Among the shin bones, the smaller one is of the shape of a bow-staff; the larger one is of the shape of the back of a python withered from hunger and thirst. The place where the shin bone is established in the ankle bones is of the shape of a date-palm shoot with its skin removed. The place where the shin bone is established in the knee bone is of the shape of the head of a mudiṅga drum. The knee bone, on one side, is of the shape of a potter's rib. The thigh bones are of the shape of a roughly hewn adze-axe handle. The place where the thigh bone is established in the hip bone is of the shape of a goldsmith's fire tongs. The place where it is established is of the shape of a punnāga fruit with its tip cut off. The two hip bones, being joined together, are of the shape of the pinnacle of a potter's wheel; some also say they are of the shape of an ascetic's water-strainer. The sitting bones are of the shape of a cobra's hood placed facing downwards. The eighteen spinal column bones, perforated in seven or eight places, are, from the inside, of the shape of a flat-headed hand-drill placed in layers, and from the outside, they are of the shape of a round bamboo joint. In between them are two or three thorns similar to the teeth of a saw. Among the twenty-four rib bones, the complete ones are of the shape of a full Sinhalese sickle, and the incomplete ones are of the shape of an incomplete Sinhalese sickle; some also say that all of them are of the shape of the two outstretched wings of a white cock. The fourteen breastbones are of the shape of a row of planks on an old palanquin. The heart bone is of the shape of the bowl of a ladle. The collarbones are of the shape of the handle of a small iron adze. Below them, the bone is of the shape of a half-moon. The shoulder blades are of the shape of an axe blade; some also say they are of the shape of a Sinhalese hoe cut in half. The arm bones are of the shape of a mirror handle; some also say they are of the shape of a large adze handle. The forearm bones are of the shape of a pair of palmyra bulbs. The wrist bones are of the shape of a flat, coiled bracelet, placed stuck together. The bones of the dorsum of the hand are of the shape of a heap of tendons from a pounded kandala plant. The base joint bones of the fingers are of the shape of a paṇava drum, the middle joint bones are of the shape of an incomplete jackfruit seed, and the tip joint bones are of the shape of a clearing-nut seed (kataka). The seven neck bones are of the shape of pieces of bamboo shoot, pierced with a rod and placed in sequence. The lower jawbone is of the shape of a blacksmith's tongs. The upper jawbone is of the shape of the loop of a small knife for peeling sugarcane rind. The bones of the eye and nose sockets are of the shape of a young palmyra seed from which the pulp has been removed. The forehead bone is of the shape of a piece of a broken conch shell placed facing downwards. The bones at the top of the ears are of the shape of a barber's razor case. Above the forehead and the bones at the top of the ears, in the place where a headband is tied, the bone is of the shape of a piece of worn cloth stretched over a thick-rimmed water pot. The crown bone is of the shape of a bent coconut with its opening cut. The skull bones are of the shape of an old, stitched-together gourd-vessel. By way of direction, they are found in two directions.

Okāsato avisesena sakalasarīre ṭhitāni, visesena tu sīsaṭṭhīni gīvaṭṭhikesu patiṭṭhitāni, gīvaṭṭhīni piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṭṭhīsu patiṭṭhitāni, piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṭṭhīni kaṭiṭṭhīsu patiṭṭhitāni, kaṭiṭṭhīni ūruṭṭhikesu patiṭṭhitāni, uruṭṭhīni jaṇṇukaṭṭhikesu, jaṇṇukaṭṭhīni jaṅghaṭṭhikesu, jaṅghaṭṭhīni gopphakaṭṭhikesu, gopphakaṭṭhīni piṭṭhipādaṭṭhikesu patiṭṭhitāni, piṭṭhipādaṭṭhikāni ca gopphakaṭṭhīni ukkhipitvā ṭhitāni, gopphakaṭṭhīni jaṅghaṭṭhīni…pe… gīvaṭṭhīni sīsaṭṭhīni ukkhipitvā ṭhitānīti etenānusārena avasesānipi aṭṭhīni veditabbāni.

By way of location, they are situated throughout the entire body without distinction. Specifically, however, the skull bones are established on the neck bones, the neck bones on the spinal column bones, the spinal column bones on the hip bones, the hip bones on the thigh bones, the thigh bones on the knee bones, the knee bones on the shin bones, the shin bones on the ankle bones, and the ankle bones on the bones of the dorsum of the foot. And the bones of the dorsum of the foot stand supporting the ankle bones; the ankle bones support the shin bones... and so on... the neck bones stand supporting the skull bones. In this way, the remaining bones should also be understood.

Tattha yathā iṭṭhakagopānasicayādīsu na uparimā iṭṭhakādayo jānanti “mayaṃ heṭṭhimesu patiṭṭhitā”ti, napi heṭṭhimā jānanti “mayaṃ uparimāni ukkhipitvā ṭhitā”ti; evameva na sīsaṭṭhikāni jānanti “mayaṃ gīvaṭṭhikesu [M 0.0040] patiṭṭhitānī”ti…pe… na gopphakaṭṭhikāni jānanti “mayaṃ piṭṭhipādaṭṭhikesu patiṭṭhitānī”ti, napi piṭṭhipādaṭṭhikāni jānanti “mayaṃ gopphakaṭṭhīni ukkhipitvā ṭhitānī”ti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Kevalaṃ tu imāni sādhikāni tīṇi aṭṭhisatāni navahi nhārusatehi navahi ca [V 0.0039] maṃsapesisatehi ābaddhānulittāni, ekaghanacammapariyonaddhāni, sattarasaharaṇīsahassānugatasinehasinehitāni, navanavutilomakūpasahassaparissavamānasedajallikāni asītikimikulāni, kāyotveva saṅkhyaṃ gatāni, yaṃ sabhāvato upaparikkhanto yogāvacaro na kiñci gayhūpagaṃ passati, kevalaṃ tu nhārusambandhaṃ nānākuṇapasaṅkiṇṇaṃ [P 0.0052] aṭṭhisaṅghāṭameva passati. Yaṃ disvā dasabalassa puttabhāvaṃ upeti. Yathāha –

Therein, just as in the case of things such as stacked bricks and rafters, the upper bricks do not know, 'We are established on the lower ones,' nor do the lower ones know, 'We, having carried the upper ones, stand'; in the same way, the skull bones do not know, 'We are established on the neck bones,'… and so on… the ankle bones do not know, 'We are established on the back-of-the-foot bones,' nor do the back-of-the-foot bones know, 'We, having carried the ankle bones, stand.' For these phenomena are devoid of adverting and reviewing… they are not a person. But merely, these over three hundred bones, bound and smeared by nine hundred sinews and nine hundred pieces of flesh, enveloped by a single solid skin, moistened by the fat that follows the seventeen thousand vessels, wet with the sweat oozing from ninety-nine thousand hair-pores, and in which eighty families of worms are established, have come to be designated as a 'body.' When a yogi investigates this according to its intrinsic nature, they see nothing whatsoever to be grasped, but merely a framework of bones bound by sinews and filled with various kinds of foul things. Seeing this, they attain the state of being a son of the Ten-Powered One. As it is said:

“Paṭipāṭiyaṭṭhīni ṭhitāni koṭiyā,

Anekasandhiyamito na kehici;

Baddho nahārūhi jarāya codito,

Acetano kaṭṭhakaliṅgarūpamo.

“Bones stand in a row, end to end,

Joined at many joints, not by anything;

Bound by sinews, impelled by decay,

Without consciousness, like a log of wood.

“Kuṇapaṃ kuṇape jātaṃ, asucimhi ca pūtini;

Duggandhe cāpi duggandhaṃ, bhedanamhi ca vayadhammaṃ.

“A corpse born of a corpse, from the impure it is putrid;

From the foul-smelling, it is foul-smelling, and in what is subject to breaking up, it is of a nature to perish.

“Aṭṭhipuṭe aṭṭhipuṭo, nibbatto pūtini pūtikāyamhi;

Tamhi ca vinetha chandaṃ, hessatha puttā dasabalassā”ti ca.

“In a framework of bones, a framework of bones is produced; in a putrid thing, in a putrid body.

In that, you should dispel desire, and you will become sons of the Ten-Powered One.”

Paricchedato anto aṭṭhimiñjena uparito maṃsena agge mūle ca aññamaññena paricchinnānīti vavatthapeti. Ayametesaṃ sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ aṭṭhīni vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

By way of delimitation, one determines: they are delimited internally by bone marrow, externally above by flesh, and at the tip and at the root by one another. This is their delimitation by common characteristic. The delimitation by dissimilar characteristic, however, is just like that of the hair. In this way, one determines the bones by way of color and other aspects.

Tato paraṃ sarīre yathāvuttappabhedānaṃ aṭṭhīnaṃ abbhantaragataṃ aṭṭhimiñjaṃ vaṇṇato setanti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato attano okāsasaṇṭhānanti. Seyyathidaṃ – mahantamahantānaṃ aṭṭhīnaṃ abbhantaragataṃ sedetvā vaṭṭetvā mahantesu vaṃsanaḷakapabbesu pakkhittamahāvettaṅkurasaṇṭhānaṃ, khuddānukhuddakānaṃ [M 0.0041] abbhantaragataṃ sedetvā vaṭṭetvā khuddānukhuddakesu vaṃsanaḷakapabbesu pakkhittatanuvettaṅkurasaṇṭhānanti. Disato dvīsu disāsu jātaṃ. Okāsato aṭṭhīnaṃ abbhantare patiṭṭhitanti.

Thereafter, one determines that the bone marrow, which is located inside the bones of the aforementioned kinds in the body, is white by way of color. By way of shape, its shape follows its location. That is to say: that which is inside very large bones has the shape of a large rattan shoot placed inside large bamboo or reed joints, as if boiled and rolled; that which is inside very small bones has the shape of a slender rattan shoot placed inside very small bamboo or reed joints, as if boiled and rolled. By way of direction, it is born in two directions. By way of location, it is established inside the bones.

Tattha yathā veḷunaḷakādīnaṃ antogatāni dadhiphāṇitāni na jānanti “mayaṃ veḷunaḷakādīnaṃ antogatānī”ti, napi veḷunaḷakādayo jānanti “dadhiphāṇitāni amhākaṃ antogatānī”ti; evameva na aṭṭhimiñjaṃ jānāti “ahaṃ aṭṭhīnaṃ antogata”nti, napi aṭṭhīni [V 0.0040] jānanti “aṭṭhimiñjaṃ amhākaṃ antogata”nti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato aṭṭhīnaṃ abbhantaratalehi [P 0.0053] aṭṭhimiñjabhāgena ca paricchinnanti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ aṭṭhimiñjaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as the curd and molasses inside bamboo and reeds do not know, 'We are inside bamboo and reeds,' nor do the bamboo and reeds know, 'Curd and molasses are inside us'; in the same way, the bone marrow does not know, 'I am inside the bones,' nor do the bones know, 'The bone marrow is inside us.' For these phenomena are devoid of adverting and reviewing… they are not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines it as delimited by the inner surfaces of the bones and by the part that is bone marrow. This is its delimitation by common characteristic. The delimitation by dissimilar characteristic, however, is just like that of the hair. In this way, one determines the bone marrow by way of color and other aspects.

Tato paraṃ sarīrassa abbhantare dvigoḷakappabhedaṃ vakkaṃ vaṇṇato mandarattaṃ pāḷibhaddakaṭṭhivaṇṇanti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato gāmadārakānaṃ suttāvutakīḷāgoḷakasaṇṭhānaṃ, ekavaṇṭasahakāradvayasaṇṭhānantipi eke. Disato uparimāya disāya jātaṃ. Okāsato galavāṭakā vinikkhantena ekamūlena thokaṃ gantvā dvidhā bhinnena thūlanhārunā vinibaddhaṃ hutvā hadayamaṃsaṃ parikkhipitvā ṭhitanti.

Thereafter, within the body, one determines the kidneys, which are distinguished as a pair of globes, to be slightly red by way of color, having a color like that of a coral tree seed. By way of shape, they have the shape of a play-ball woven with thread by village children; some say they also have the shape of a pair of mangoes on a single stalk. By way of direction, they are born in the upper direction. By way of location, they stand surrounding the heart-flesh, bound by a thick sinew which, having emerged from the throat region with a single root and gone a little way, splits in two.

Tattha yathā vaṇṭūpanibaddhaṃ sahakāradvayaṃ na jānāti “ahaṃ vaṇṭena upanibaddha”nti, napi vaṇṭaṃ jānāti “mayā sahakāradvayaṃ upanibaddha”nti; evameva na vakkaṃ jānāti “ahaṃ thūlanhārunā upanibaddha”nti, napi thūlanhāru jānāti “mayā vakkaṃ upanibaddha”nti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato vakkaṃ vakkabhāgena paricchinnanti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ vakkaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as a pair of mangoes bound to a stalk does not know, 'I am bound by the stalk,' nor does the stalk know, 'The pair of mangoes is bound by me'; in the same way, the kidney does not know, 'I am bound by the thick sinew,' nor does the thick sinew know, 'The kidney is bound by me.' For these phenomena are devoid of adverting and reviewing… they are not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines the kidney as delimited by the kidney-part. This is its delimitation by common characteristic. The delimitation by dissimilar characteristic, however, is just like that of the hair. In this way, one determines the kidney by way of color and other aspects.

Tato paraṃ sarīrassa abbhantare hadayaṃ vaṇṇato rattaṃ rattapadumapattapiṭṭhivaṇṇanti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato bāhirapattāni apanetvā adhomukhaṭhapitapadumamakuḷasaṇṭhānaṃ, tañca aggacchinnapunnāgaphalamiva vivaṭekapassaṃ bahi maṭṭhaṃ anto kosātakīphalassa abbhantarasadisaṃ. Paññābahulānaṃ thokaṃ [M 0.0042] vikasitaṃ, mandapaññānaṃ makuḷitameva. Yaṃ rūpaṃ nissāya manodhātu ca manoviññāṇadhātu ca pavattanti, taṃ apanetvā avasesamaṃsapiṇḍasaṅkhātahadayabbhantare addhapasatamattaṃ [P 0.0054] lohitaṃ saṇṭhāti, taṃ rāgacaritassa rattaṃ, dosacaritassa kāḷakaṃ, mohacaritassa maṃsadhovanodakasadisaṃ, vitakkacaritassa kulatthayūsavaṇṇaṃ, saddhācaritassa kaṇikārapupphavaṇṇaṃ, paññācaritassa acchaṃ vippasannamanāvilaṃ, niddhotajātimaṇi viya jutimantaṃ khāyati. Disato uparimāya disāya jātaṃ. Okāsato sarīrabbhantare dvinnaṃ thanānaṃ majjhe patiṭṭhitanti.

Thereafter, within the body, one determines the heart: by color, it is red, the color of the back of a red lotus petal. By shape, it is like a lotus bud with its outer petals removed, placed facing downwards; and it is like a punnāga fruit with its tip cut off, open on one side, smooth on the outside, and on the inside like the interior of a kosātakī fruit. For those of great wisdom, it is slightly open; for those of dull wisdom, it is merely a bud. Setting aside that form upon which the mind-element and the mind-consciousness-element depend, within the heart—which is reckoned as the remaining lump of flesh—about half a pasata of blood is established. This blood is red for one of a lustful temperament; black for one of a hateful temperament; like water used to wash meat for one of a deluded temperament; the color of horse gram soup for one of a speculative temperament; the color of a kaṇikāra flower for one of a faithful temperament. For one of a wise temperament, it appears clear, very bright, untroubled, and radiant like a polished, genuine gem. By direction, it arises in the upper direction. By location, it is established within the body, between the two breasts.

Tattha yathā dvinnaṃ vātapānakavāṭakānaṃ majjhe ṭhito aggaḷatthambhako na jānāti “ahaṃ dvinnaṃ [V 0.0041] vātapānakavāṭakānaṃ majjhe ṭhito”ti, napi vātapānakavāṭakāni jānanti “amhākaṃ majjhe aggaḷatthambhako ṭhito”ti; evamevaṃ na hadayaṃ jānāti “ahaṃ dvinnaṃ thanānaṃ majjhe ṭhita”nti, napi thanāni jānanti “hadayaṃ amhākaṃ majjhe ṭhita”nti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato hadayaṃ hadayabhāgena paricchinnanti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ hadayaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as a locking-post standing between two window panels does not know, 'I am standing between two window panels,' nor do the window panels know, 'A locking-post is standing between us'; in the very same way, the heart does not know, 'I am situated between the two breasts,' nor do the breasts know, 'The heart is situated between us.' For these phenomena are devoid of directing the mind and reviewing... not a person. By delimitation, one determines: 'The heart is delimited by the heart-portion.' This is its delimitation by similar nature. But its delimitation by dissimilar nature is just like that of the hair. Thus, one determines the heart by way of color and so on.

Tato paraṃ sarīrassa abbhantare yakanasaññitaṃ yamakamaṃsapiṇḍaṃ vaṇṇato rattaṃ rattakumudabāhirapattapiṭṭhivaṇṇanti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato ekamūlaṃ hutvā agge yamakaṃ koviḷārapattasaṇṭhānaṃ, tañca dandhānaṃ ekaṃyeva hoti mahantaṃ, paññavantānaṃ dve vā tīṇi vā khuddakānīti. Disato uparimāya disāya jātaṃ. Okāsato dvinnaṃ thanānaṃ abbhantare dakkhiṇapassaṃ nissāya ṭhitanti.

Thereafter, within the body, one determines the twin lump of flesh designated as the liver: by color, it is red, the color of the back of an outer petal of a red water lily. By shape, having a single root, it is paired at the tip, having the shape of a koviḷāra leaf; and for those of dull intellect, it is just one and is large, while for the wise, there are two or three, and they are small. By direction, it arises in the upper direction. By location, it is situated within, between the two breasts, depending on the right side.

Tattha yathā piṭharakapasse laggā maṃsapesi na jānāti “ahaṃ piṭharakapasse laggā”ti, napi piṭharakapassaṃ jānāti “mayi maṃsapesi laggā”ti; evameva na yakanaṃ jānāti “ahaṃ dvinnaṃ thanānaṃ abbhantare dakkhiṇapassaṃ nissāya ṭhita”nti, napi thanānaṃ abbhantare dakkhiṇapassaṃ jānāti “maṃ nissāya yakanaṃ ṭhita”nti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato pana yakanaṃ yakanabhāgena [M 0.0043] paricchinnanti vavatthapeti[P 0.0055]. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ yakanaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as a piece of meat stuck to the side of a pot does not know, 'I am stuck to the side of a pot,' nor does the side of the pot know, 'A piece of meat is stuck to me'; in the very same way, the liver does not know, 'I am situated within, between the two breasts, depending on the right side,' nor does the right side within, between the two breasts, know, 'The liver is situated depending on me.' For these phenomena are devoid of directing the mind and reviewing... not a person. By delimitation, however, one determines: 'The liver is delimited by the liver-portion.' This is its delimitation by similar nature. But its delimitation by dissimilar nature is just like that of the hair. Thus, one determines the liver by way of color and so on.

Tato paraṃ sarīre paṭicchannāpaṭicchannabhedato duvidhaṃ kilomakaṃ vaṇṇato setaṃ dukūlapilotikavaṇṇanti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato attano okāsasaṇṭhānaṃ. Disato dvīsu disāsu jātaṃ. Okāsato paṭicchannakilomakaṃ hadayañca vakkañca parivāretvā, appaṭicchannakilomakaṃ sakalasarīre cammassa heṭṭhato maṃsaṃ pariyonandhitvā ṭhitanti.

Thereafter, in the body, one determines the membrane, which is of two kinds by the distinction of covering and non-covering: by color, it is white, the color of fine cloth or a worn cloth. By shape, it has the shape of its own location. By direction, it arises in two directions. By location, the covering membrane is situated surrounding the heart and the kidneys, while the non-covering membrane is situated throughout the entire body beneath the skin, enveloping the flesh.

Tattha yathā pilotikāya paliveṭhite maṃse na pilotikā jānāti “mayā maṃsaṃ paliveṭhita”nti, napi maṃsaṃ jānāti “ahaṃ pilotikāya paliveṭhita”nti; evameva na kilomakaṃ jānāti “mayā hadayavakkāni sakalasarīre ca cammassa heṭṭhato maṃsaṃ paliveṭhita”nti. Napi hadayavakkāni sakalasarīre ca maṃsaṃ jānāti “ahaṃ kilomakena paliveṭhita”nti[V 0.0042]. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato heṭṭhā maṃsena upari cammena tiriyaṃ kilomakabhāgena paricchinnanti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ kilomakaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as when flesh is wrapped in a piece of cloth, the cloth does not know, 'I have wrapped the flesh,' nor does the flesh know, 'I am wrapped by the cloth'; in the very same way, the membrane does not know, 'I have wrapped the heart and kidneys, and the flesh beneath the skin throughout the entire body.' Nor do the heart and kidneys, and the flesh throughout the entire body, know, 'We are wrapped by the membrane.' For these phenomena are devoid of directing the mind and reviewing... not a person. By delimitation, one determines: 'It is delimited below by the flesh, above by the skin, and across by the membrane-portion.' This is its delimitation by similar nature. But its delimitation by dissimilar nature is just like that of the hair. Thus, one determines the membrane by way of color and so on.

Tato paraṃ sarīrassa abbhantare pihakaṃ vaṇṇato nīlaṃ mīlātanigguṇḍīpupphavaṇṇanti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato yebhuyyena sattaṅgulappamāṇaṃ abandhanaṃ kāḷavacchakajivhāsaṇṭhānaṃ. Disato uparimāya disāya jātaṃ. Okāsato hadayassa vāmapasse udarapaṭalassa matthakapassaṃ nissāya ṭhitaṃ, yamhi paharaṇapahārena bahi nikkhante sattānaṃ jīvitakkhayo hotīti.

Thereafter, within the body, one determines the spleen: by color, it is dark blue, the color of a faded nigguṇḍī flower. By shape, it is for the most part the measure of seven finger-breadths, unattached, and has the shape of a black calf's tongue. By direction, it arises in the upper direction. By location, it is situated on the left side of the heart, depending on the upper surface of the stomach membrane; and when this is struck by a weapon and comes out, for beings, there is the destruction of life.

Tattha yathā koṭṭhakamatthakapassaṃ nissāya ṭhitā na gomayapiṇḍi jānāti “ahaṃ koṭṭhakamatthakapassaṃ nissāya ṭhitā”ti, napi koṭṭhakamatthakapassaṃ jānāti “gomayapiṇḍi maṃ nissāya ṭhitā”ti; evameva na pihakaṃ jānāti “ahaṃ udarapaṭalassa matthakapassaṃ nissāya ṭhita”nti, napi udarapaṭalassa matthakapassaṃ jānāti “pihakaṃ maṃ nissāya ṭhita”nti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato [M 0.0044] pihakaṃ pihakabhāgena [P 0.0056] paricchinnanti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ pihakaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as a lump of cow-dung relying on the outside of a granary wall does not know, 'I am situated relying on the outside of a granary wall,' nor does the outside of the granary wall know, 'A lump of cow-dung is situated relying on me'; even so, the spleen does not know, 'I am situated relying on the upper surface of the abdominal lining,' nor does the upper surface of the abdominal lining know, 'The spleen is situated relying on me.' Indeed, these phenomena are devoid of adverting and reviewing... not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines: 'The spleen is delimited by the spleen-part.' This is its homogeneous delimitation. The heterogeneous delimitation, however, is just like that of the hair. In this way, one determines the spleen by way of color and so forth.

Tato paraṃ sarīrassa abbhantare dvattiṃsamaṃsakhaṇḍappabhedaṃ papphāsaṃ vaṇṇato rattaṃ nātiparipakkaudumbaravaṇṇanti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato visamacchinnapūvasaṇṭhānaṃ, chadaniṭṭhakakhaṇḍapuñjasaṇṭhānantipi eke. Tadetaṃ abbhantare asitapītādīnaṃ abhāve uggatena kammajatejusmanā abbhāhatattā saṅkhāditapalālapiṇḍamiva nirasaṃ nirojaṃ hoti. Disato uparimāya disāya jātaṃ. Okāsato sarīrabbhantare dvinnaṃ thanānaṃ abbhantare hadayañca yakanañca upari chādetvā olambantaṃ ṭhitanti.

After that, one determines the lungs—a division of the thirty-two flesh-parts within the body—as follows: By color, they are red, the color of a not-too-ripe udumbara fruit. By shape, they have the shape of an unevenly cut cake; some say they have the shape of a pile of broken roof-tiles. Due to the absence of things eaten, drunk, etc., within, and because of being afflicted by the vapor of the kamma-born heat element that has arisen, they become juiceless and without nutritive essence, like a pressed-down heap of straw. By direction, they arise in the upper direction. By location, they are situated inside the body, between the two breasts, hanging down and covering the heart and the liver from above.

Tattha yathā jiṇṇakoṭṭhabbhantare lambamāno sakuṇakulāvako na jānāti “ahaṃ jiṇṇakoṭṭhabbhantare lambamāno ṭhito”ti, napi jiṇṇakoṭṭhabbhantaraṃ jānāti “sakuṇakulāvako mayi lambamāno ṭhito”ti; evameva na papphāsaṃ jānāti “ahaṃ sarīrabbhantare dvinnaṃ thanānaṃ antare lambamānaṃ ṭhita”nti, napi sarīrabbhantare dvinnaṃ thanānaṃ antaraṃ jānāti “mayi papphāsaṃ lambamānaṃ ṭhita”nti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato [V 0.0043] papphāsaṃ papphāsabhāgena paricchinnanti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ papphāsaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as a bird's nest hanging inside an old granary does not know, 'I am situated hanging inside an old granary,' nor does the inside of the old granary know, 'A bird's nest is situated hanging in me'; even so, the lungs do not know, 'I am situated hanging inside the body between the two breasts,' nor does the space inside the body between the two breasts know, 'The lungs are situated hanging in me.' Indeed, these phenomena are devoid of adverting and reviewing... not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines: 'The lungs are delimited by the lung-part.' This is its homogeneous delimitation. The heterogeneous delimitation, however, is just like that of the hair. In this way, one determines the lungs by way of color and so forth.

Tato paraṃ antosarīre purisassa dvattiṃsahatthaṃ, itthiyā aṭṭhavīsatihatthaṃ, ekavīsatiyā ṭhānesu obhaggaṃ antaṃ vaṇṇato setaṃ sakkharasudhāvaṇṇanti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato sīsaṃ chinditvā lohitadoṇiyaṃ saṃvelletvā ṭhapitadhammanisaṇṭhānaṃ. Disato dvīsu disāsu jātaṃ. Okāsato upari galavāṭake heṭṭhā ca karīsamagge vinibandhattā galavāṭakakarīsamaggapariyante sarīrabbhantare [P 0.0057] ṭhitanti.

After that, one determines the large intestine within the body as follows: For a man, it is thirty-two cubits; for a woman, twenty-eight cubits; and it is bent in twenty-one places. By color, it is white, the color of plaster stone. By shape, it has the shape of a python that has had its head cut off, been coiled, and placed in a blood-washing trough. By direction, it arises in two directions. By location, because it is bound above at the throat opening and below in the path of excrement, it is situated inside the body, between the limits of the throat opening and the path of excrement.

Tattha yathā lohitadoṇiyaṃ ṭhapitaṃ chinnasīsaṃ dhammanikaḷevaraṃ na jānāti “ahaṃ lohitadoṇiyaṃ ṭhita”nti, napi lohitadoṇi jānāti “mayi chinnasīsaṃ dhammanikaḷevaraṃ ṭhita”nti; evameva na antaṃ jānāti “ahaṃ sarīrabbhantare ṭhita”nti, napi sarīrabbhantaraṃ jānāti “mayi antaṃ ṭhita”nti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā [M 0.0045] hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato antaṃ antabhāgena paricchinnanti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ antaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as the body of a python with its head cut off, placed in a blood-washing trough, does not know, 'I am situated in a blood-washing trough,' nor does the blood-washing trough know, 'The body of a python with its head cut off is situated in me'; even so, the large intestine does not know, 'I am situated inside the body,' nor does the inside of the body know, 'The large intestine is situated in me.' Indeed, these phenomena are devoid of adverting and reviewing... not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines: 'The large intestine is delimited by the large intestine-part.' This is its homogeneous delimitation. The heterogeneous delimitation, however, is just like that of the hair. In this way, one determines the large intestine by way of color and so forth.

Tato paraṃ antosarīre antantare antaguṇaṃ vaṇṇato setaṃ dakasītalikamūlavaṇṇanti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato dakasītalikamūlasaṇṭhānamevāti, gomuttasaṇṭhānantipi eke. Disato dvīsu disāsu jātaṃ. Okāsato kudālapharasukammādīni karontānaṃ yantākaḍḍhanakāle yantasuttakamiva yantaphalakāni antabhoge ekato aggaḷante ābandhitvā pādapuñchanarajjumaṇḍalakassa antarā taṃ sibbitvā ṭhitarajjukā viya ekavīsatiyā antabhogānaṃ antarā ṭhitanti.

After that, one determines the intestinal mesentery within the body, between the large intestines, as follows: By color, it is white, the color of the root of the dakasītalika plant. By shape, it is just like the shape of the root of the dakasītalika plant; some say it has the shape of cow's urine. By direction, it arises in two directions. By location, it is situated between the twenty-one coils of the large intestine, like the rope of a machine when those performing tasks with hoes, axes, etc., are pulling the machine, or like a rope sewn and placed between the circle of a foot-wiping rope-mat, having bound machine-planks to the coils at one end with a bolt.

Tattha yathā pādapuñchanarajjumaṇḍalakaṃ sibbitvā ṭhitarajjukā na jānāti “mayā pādapuñchanarajjumaṇḍalakaṃ sibbita”nti, napi pādapuñchanarajjumaṇḍalakaṃ jānāti “rajjukā maṃ sibbitvā ṭhitā”ti, evameva antaguṇaṃ na jānāti “ahaṃ antaṃ ekavīsatibhogabbhantare ābandhitvā ṭhita”nti, napi antaṃ jānāti “antaguṇaṃ maṃ ābandhitvā ṭhita”nti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato antaguṇaṃ antaguṇabhāgena [V 0.0044] paricchinnanti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ antaguṇaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as a rope that is placed having sewn a foot-wiping rope-mat does not know, 'I have sewn a foot-wiping rope-mat,' nor does the foot-wiping rope-mat know, 'A rope is situated having sewn me'; even so, the intestinal mesentery does not know, 'I am situated having bound the large intestine between its twenty-one coils,' nor does the large intestine know, 'The intestinal mesentery is situated having bound me.' Indeed, these phenomena are devoid of adverting and reviewing... not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines: 'The intestinal mesentery is delimited by the intestinal mesentery-part.' This is its homogeneous delimitation. The heterogeneous delimitation, however, is just like that of the hair. In this way, one determines the intestinal mesentery by way of color and so forth.

Tato paraṃ antosarīre udariyaṃ vaṇṇato ajjhohaṭāhāravaṇṇanti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato parissāvane sithilabaddhataṇḍulasaṇṭhānaṃ. Disato uparimāya disāya jātaṃ. Okāsato udare ṭhitanti[P 0.0058]. Udaraṃ nāma ubhato nippīḷiyamānassa allasāṭakassa majjhe sañjātaphoṭakasadisaṃ antapaṭalaṃ, bahi maṭṭhaṃ, anto maṃsakasambupaliveṭhitaṃ, kiliṭṭhapāvārapupphasadisaṃ, kuthitapanasaphalassa abbhantarasadisantipi eke. Tattha takkolakā gaṇḍuppādakātālahīrakāsūcimukhakāpaṭatantusuttakāti evamādidvattiṃsakulappabhedā kimayo ākulabyākulā saṇḍasaṇḍacārino hutvā nivasanti, ye pānabhojanādimhi avijjamāne ullaṅghitvā viravantā [M 0.0046] hadayamaṃsaṃ abhitudanti pānabhojanādīni ajjhoharaṇavelāyañca uddhaṃmukhā hutvā paṭhamajjhohaṭe dve tayo ālope turitaturitā vilumpanti. Yaṃ etesaṃ kimīnaṃ pasūtigharaṃ vaccakuṭi gilānasālā susānañca hoti, yattha seyyathāpi nāma caṇḍālagāmadvāre candanikāya saradasamaye thūlaphusitake deve vassante udakena āvūḷhaṃ muttakarīsacammaṭṭhinhārukhaṇḍakheḷasiṅghāṇikālohitappabhutinānākuṇapajātaṃ nipatitvā kaddamodakāluḷitaṃ sañjātakimikulākulaṃ hutvā dvīhatīhaccayena sūriyātapasantāpavegakuthitaṃ upari pheṇapupphuḷake muñcantaṃ abhinīlavaṇṇaṃ paramaduggandhajegucchaṃ upagantuṃ vā daṭṭhuṃ vā anaraharūpataṃ āpajjitvā tiṭṭhati, pageva ghāyituṃ vā sāyituṃ vā; evameva nānappakārapānabhojanādi dantamusalasaṃcuṇṇitaṃ jivhāhatthasamparivattitaṃ kheḷalālāpalibuddhaṃ taṅkhaṇavigatavaṇṇagandharasādisampadaṃ koliyakhalisuvānavamathusadisaṃ nipatitvā pittasemhavātapaliveṭhitaṃ hutvā udaraggisantāpavegakuthitaṃ kimikulākulaṃ uparūpari pheṇapupphuḷakāni muñcantaṃ paramakasambuduggandhajegucchabhāvamāpajjitvā tiṭṭhati. Yaṃ sutvāpi [P 0.0059] pānabhojanādīsu amanuññatā saṇṭhāti, pageva paññācakkhunā oloketvā. Yattha ca patitaṃ pānabhojanādi pañcadhā vivekaṃ gacchati, ekaṃ bhāgaṃ pāṇakā khādanti, ekaṃ bhāgaṃ udaraggi jhāpeti, eko bhāgo muttaṃ hoti, eko bhāgo karīsaṃ hoti, eko bhāgo rasabhāvaṃ āpajjitvā soṇitamaṃsādīni upabrūhayatīti.

Then, further, within the body, one defines the stomach contents by color as having the color of swallowed food. By shape, they are like a loosely tied bundle of rice in a water strainer. By direction, they originate from the upper region. By location, they are situated in the stomach. The stomach is an inner membrane like a blister formed in the middle of a wet cloth being squeezed from both sides—smooth on the outside, and on the inside smeared with flesh like that of a snail, resembling the flower pattern on a soiled shawl. Some say it is also like the inside of a rotten jackfruit. There, thirty-two kinds of worms, such as takkolakā, gaṇḍuppādakā, tālahīrakā, sūcimukhakā, and paṭatantusuttakā, dwell in a state of confusion and disorder, moving about in swarms. When there is no food or drink, they jump up, crying out and pecking at the heart-flesh. And at the time of swallowing food and drink, with faces upturned, they hastily snatch the first two or three mouthfuls that are swallowed. This stomach content is the birthing place of these worms, and it is also a latrine, a sick-room, and a charnel ground. It is like this: at the gate of an outcaste village, in a cesspool, during the autumn season when heavy rain falls, various kinds of corpses—such as urine, feces, skin, bones, pieces of sinew, phlegm, mucus, and blood—are swept along by the water, fall in, and become turbid with mud and water, teeming with swarms of worms. After two or three days, putrefied by the intense heat of the sun, it emits froth and bubbles from its surface, becomes deep blue in color, and is so extremely foul-smelling and disgusting that it becomes unfit to approach or even to look at—how much more so to smell or to taste. In the same way, various kinds of food and drink, ground to powder by the pestle of the teeth, turned over by the hand of the tongue, smeared with spittle and saliva, instantly losing their qualities of color, smell, and taste, fall down like dog's vomit in a trough of the Koliyans. Being enveloped by bile, phlegm, and wind, putrefied by the intense heat of the stomach-fire, teeming with swarms of worms, emitting froth and bubbles from its surface, it reaches a state of extreme filth, foul odor, and loathsomeness. Merely hearing of this establishes displeasure towards food and drink—how much more so when seeing it with the eye of wisdom. And there, the food and drink that have fallen undergo a fivefold separation: one part the creatures eat; one part the stomach-fire burns up; one part becomes urine; one part becomes feces; and one part, becoming nutrient essence, nourishes the blood, flesh, and so on.

Tattha yathā paramajegucchāya suvānadoṇiyā ṭhito suvānavamathu na jānāti “ahaṃ suvānadoṇiyā ṭhito”ti; napi suvānadoṇi jānāti “mayi suvānavamathu ṭhito”ti. Evameva na udariyaṃ jānāti “ahaṃ imasmiṃ paramaduggandhajegucche udare ṭhita”nti; napi udaraṃ jānāti “mayi udariyaṃ ṭhita”nti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti[V 0.0045]. Paricchedato udariyaṃ udariyabhāgena paricchinnanti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ udariyaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as dog's vomit lying in a most disgusting dog's trough does not know, 'I am lying in a dog's trough,' nor does the dog's trough know, 'Dog's vomit is lying in me'; in the same way, the stomach contents do not know, 'I am situated in this extremely foul-smelling and disgusting stomach,' nor does the stomach know, 'The stomach contents are situated in me.' Indeed, these phenomena are devoid of attending and reviewing... they are not a person. By way of delimitation, one defines the stomach contents as being delimited by the part that is stomach contents. This is its delimitation by way of a shared characteristic; its delimitation by way of a distinct characteristic, however, is just like that of the hair. In this way, one defines the stomach contents by way of color and so on.

Tato [M 0.0047] paraṃ antosarīre karīsaṃ vaṇṇato yebhuyyena ajjhohaṭāhāravaṇṇanti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato okāsasaṇṭhānaṃ, disato heṭṭhimāya disāya jātaṃ, okāsato pakkāsaye ṭhitanti. Pakkāsayo nāma heṭṭhā nābhipiṭṭhikaṇṭakamūlānaṃ antare antāvasāne ubbedhena aṭṭhaṅgulamatto vaṃsanaḷakabbhantarasadiso padeso, yattha seyyathāpi nāma uparibhūmibhāge patitaṃ vassodakaṃ ogaḷitvā heṭṭhābhūmibhāgaṃ pūretvā tiṭṭhati, evameva yaṃkiñci āmāsaye patitaṃ pānabhojanādikaṃ udaragginā pheṇuddehakaṃ pakkaṃ pakkaṃ saṇhakaraṇiyā piṭṭhamiva saṇhabhāvaṃ āpajjitvā antabilena ogaḷitvā omadditvā vaṃsanaḷake pakkhittapaṇḍumattikā viya sannicitaṃ hutvā tiṭṭhati.

Then, further, within the body, one defines feces as being, for the most part, the color of the swallowed food. By shape, they have the shape of their location. By direction, they originate from the lower region. By location, they are situated in the receptacle for digested food. The receptacle for digested food is a region about eight finger-breadths in height, like the inside of a bamboo tube, located below, between the navel and the base of the spine, at the end of the intestines. Therein, just as rainwater that has fallen on higher ground flows down, fills the lower ground, and remains there; in the same way, whatever food and drink has fallen into the stomach, being cooked again and again by the stomach-fire and brought to a froth, reaches a fine state like flour by the fine-making process, flows down through the intestinal opening, is pressed down, and remains there, accumulated like pale clay packed into a bamboo tube.

Tattha yathā vaṃsanaḷake omadditvā pakkhittapaṇḍumattikā na jānāti “ahaṃ vaṃsanaḷake ṭhitā”ti, napi vaṃsanaḷako jānāti “mayi paṇḍumattikā ṭhitā”ti; evameva na karīsaṃ jānāti [P 0.0060] “ahaṃ pakkāsaye ṭhita”nti, napi pakkāsayo jānāti “mayi karīsaṃ ṭhita”nti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato karīsaṃ karīsabhāgena paricchinnanti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ karīsaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as pale clay that has been pressed and packed into a bamboo tube does not know, 'I am situated in a bamboo tube,' nor does the bamboo tube know, 'Pale clay is situated in me'; in the same way, feces do not know, 'I am situated in the receptacle for digested food,' nor does the receptacle for digested food know, 'Feces are situated in me.' Indeed, these phenomena are devoid of attending and reviewing... they are not a person. By way of delimitation, one defines feces as being delimited by the part that is feces. This is its delimitation by way of a shared characteristic; its delimitation by way of a distinct characteristic, however, is just like that of the hair. In this way, one defines feces by way of color and so on.

Tato paraṃ sarīre sīsakaṭāhabbhantare matthaluṅgaṃ vaṇṇato setaṃ ahichattakapiṇḍivaṇṇanti vavatthapeti. Pakkuthitaduddhavaṇṇantipi eke. Saṇṭhānato okāsasaṇṭhānaṃ. Disato uparimāya disāya jātaṃ. Okāsato sīsakaṭāhassa abbhantare cattāro sibbinimagge nissāya samodhāya ṭhapitā cattāro piṭṭhapiṇḍikā viya samohitaṃ catumatthaluṅgapiṇḍappabhedaṃ hutvā ṭhitanti.

Then, further, within the body, inside the skull-bowl, one defines the brain as being white in color, the color of a lump of mushroom. Some say it is also the color of curdled milk. By shape, it has the shape of its location. By direction, it originates from the upper region. By location, inside the skull-bowl, resting on the four suture lines, it is situated like four lumps of dough placed together, existing as a single mass differentiated into four portions of brain-matter.

Tattha yathā purāṇalābukaṭāhe pakkhittapiṭṭhapiṇḍi pakkuthitaduddhaṃ vā na jānāti “ahaṃ purāṇalābukaṭāhe ṭhita”nti, napi purāṇalābukaṭāhaṃ jānāti “mayi piṭṭhapiṇḍi pakkuthitaduddhaṃ vā ṭhita”nti; evameva na matthaluṅgaṃ jānāti “ahaṃ sīsakaṭāhabbhantare ṭhita”nti, napi sīsakaṭāhabbhantaraṃ jānāti “mayi matthaluṅgaṃ ṭhita”nti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato matthaluṅgaṃ matthaluṅgabhāgena paricchinnanti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa [V 0.0046] sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ matthaluṅgaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as a lump of flour or foam with a bad appearance placed in an old gourd bowl does not know, “I am situated in an old gourd bowl,” nor does the old gourd bowl know, “A lump of flour or foam with a bad appearance is situated in me”; even so, the brain does not know, “I am situated inside the skull,” nor does the inside of the skull know, “The brain is situated in me.” For these phenomena are devoid of adverting and reflecting... not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines: “The brain is delimited by the brain portion.” This is its delimitation by similar characteristic; its delimitation by dissimilar characteristic, however, is just like the hair. Thus, one determines the brain by way of color, and so on.

Tato [M 0.0048] paraṃ sarīre baddhābaddhabhedato duvidhampi pittaṃ vaṇṇato bahalamadhukatelavaṇṇanti vavatthapeti. Abaddhapittaṃ milātabakulapupphavaṇṇantipi eke. Saṇṭhānato okāsasaṇṭhānaṃ. Disato dvīsu disāsu jātaṃ. Okāsato abaddhapittaṃ kesalomanakhadantānaṃ maṃsavinimuttaṭṭhānaṃ thaddhasukkhacammañca vajjetvā udakamiva telabindu avasesasarīraṃ byāpetvā ṭhitaṃ, yamhi kupite akkhīni pītakāni honti bhamanti, gattaṃ kampati kaṇḍūyati. Baddhapittaṃ hadayapapphāsānamantare [P 0.0061] yakanamaṃsaṃ nissāya patiṭṭhite mahākosātakikosakasadise pittakosake ṭhitaṃ, yamhi kupite sattā ummattakā honti, vipallatthacittā hirottappaṃ chaḍḍetvā akattabbaṃ karonti, abhāsitabbaṃ bhāsanti, acintitabbaṃ cintenti.

After that, in the body, one determines the bile, which is of two kinds by the distinction of bound and unbound, as having the color of thick madhuka-tree oil by way of color. Some say that unbound bile has the color of a faded bakula flower. By way of shape, its shape is that of its location. By way of direction, it is produced in two directions. By way of location, the unbound bile, avoiding the hair of the head, body hair, nails, teeth, places free from flesh, and tough, dry skin, pervades and is situated in the rest of the body like a drop of oil that has pervaded water. When this is agitated, the eyes become yellow and roll, the body trembles and itches. The bound bile is situated in the gall bladder, which is like the husk of a large kosātaki fruit, established depending on the liver-flesh between the heart and lungs. When this is agitated, beings become insane; with deranged minds, having abandoned moral shame and moral dread, they do what should not be done, say what should not be said, and think what should not be thought.

Tattha yathā udakaṃ byāpetvā ṭhitaṃ telaṃ na jānāti “ahaṃ udakaṃ byāpetvā ṭhita”nti, napi udakaṃ jānāti “telaṃ maṃ byāpetvā ṭhita”nti; evameva na abaddhapittaṃ jānāti “ahaṃ sarīraṃ byāpetvā ṭhita”nti, napi sarīraṃ jānāti “abaddhapittaṃ maṃ byāpetvā ṭhita”nti. Yathā ca kosātakikosake ṭhitaṃ vassodakaṃ na jānāti “ahaṃ kosātakikosake ṭhita”nti, napi kosātakikosako jānāti “mayi vassodakaṃ ṭhita”nti; evameva na baddhapittaṃ jānāti “ahaṃ pittakosake ṭhita”nti, napi pittakosako jānāti “mayi baddhapittaṃ ṭhita”nti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato pittaṃ pittabhāgena paricchinnanti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ pittaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as oil that has pervaded water does not know, “I am situated having pervaded water,” nor does the water know, “Oil is situated having pervaded me”; even so, the unbound bile does not know, “I am situated having pervaded the body,” nor does the body know, “Unbound bile is situated having pervaded me.” And just as rainwater situated in the husk of a kosātaki fruit does not know, “I am situated in the husk of a kosātaki fruit,” nor does the husk of the kosātaki fruit know, “Rainwater is situated in me”; even so, the bound bile does not know, “I am situated in the gall bladder,” nor does the gall bladder know, “Bound bile is situated in me.” For these phenomena are devoid of adverting and reflecting... not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines: “Bile is delimited by the bile portion.” This is its delimitation by similar characteristic; its delimitation by dissimilar characteristic, however, is just like the hair. Thus, one determines the bile by way of color, and so on.

Tato paraṃ sarīrabbhantare ekapattapūrappamāṇaṃ semhaṃ vaṇṇato setaṃ kacchakapaṇṇarasavaṇṇanti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato okāsasaṇṭhānaṃ. Disato uparimāya disāya jātaṃ. Okāsato udarapaṭale ṭhitanti. Yaṃ [M 0.0049] pānabhojanādiajjhoharaṇakāle seyyathāpi nāma udake sevālapaṇakaṃ kaṭṭhe vā kathale vā patante chijjitvā dvidhā hutvā puna ajjhottharitvā tiṭṭhati, evameva pānabhojanādimhi nipatante chijjitvā dvidhā hutvā puna ajjhottharitvā tiṭṭhati, yamhi ca mandībhūte pakkamiva gaṇḍaṃ pūtikamiva kukkuṭaṇḍaṃ udarapaṭalaṃ paramajegucchakuṇapagandhaṃ hoti. Tato uggatena ca gandhena uggāropi mukhampi duggandhaṃ pūtikuṇapasadisaṃ hoti, so ca puriso “apehi [V 0.0047] duggandhaṃ vāyasī”ti vattabbataṃ [P 0.0062] āpajjati, yañca abhivaḍḍhitaṃ bahalattamāpannaṃ paṭikujjanaphalakamiva vaccakuṭiyā udarapaṭalabbhantare eva kuṇapagandhaṃ sannirumbhitvā tiṭṭhati.

After that, one determines the phlegm within the body, which has the measure of a single betel chew, as being white by way of color, the color of kacchaka leaf juice. By way of shape, its shape is that of its location. By way of direction, it is produced in the upper direction. By way of location, it is situated on the surface of the stomach fluid. When drinks, food, etc., are being swallowed, just as, for instance, algae or moss in water, when a piece of wood or a potsherd falls on it, splits and becomes twofold, and then covers it over again and remains; even so, when drinks, food, etc., fall on it, it splits and becomes twofold, and then covers it over again and remains. And when it is diminished, the surface of the stomach fluid becomes extremely disgusting with the smell of a corpse, like a ripe boil or a rotten hen’s egg. And from the odor that has risen from that, the belch and also the mouth become foul-smelling, like a putrid corpse. And that person becomes liable to be told, “Go away! A foul smell emanates.” And when it has increased and become thick, it remains inside the surface of the stomach fluid, confining the corpse-like smell, like a plank covering a latrine.

Tattha yathā candanikāya uparipheṇapaṭalaṃ na jānāti “ahaṃ candanikāya ṭhita”nti, napi candanikā jānāti “mayi pheṇapaṭalaṃ ṭhita”nti; evameva na semhaṃ jānāti “ahaṃ udarapaṭale ṭhita”nti, napi udarapaṭalaṃ jānāti “mayi semhaṃ ṭhitanti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato semhaṃ semhabhāgena paricchinnanti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ semhaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as the layer of foam on a cesspool does not know, “I am situated on the cesspool,” nor does the cesspool know, “A layer of foam is situated on me”; even so, the phlegm does not know, “I am situated on the surface of the stomach fluid,” nor does the surface of the stomach fluid know, “Phlegm is situated on me.” For these phenomena are devoid of adverting and reflecting... not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines: “Phlegm is delimited by the phlegm portion.” This is its delimitation by similar characteristic; its delimitation by dissimilar characteristic, however, is just like the hair. Thus, one determines the phlegm by way of color, and so on.

Tato paraṃ sarīre pubbo vaṇṇato paṇḍupalāsavaṇṇoti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato okāsasaṇṭhāno. Disato dvīsu disāsu jāto. Okāsato pubbassa okāso nāma nibaddho natthi. Yattha pubbo sannicito tiṭṭheyya, yatra yatra khāṇukaṇṭakappaharaṇaggijālādīhi abhihate sarīrappadese lohitaṃ saṇṭhahitvā paccati, gaṇḍapiḷakādayo vā uppajjanti, tatra tatra tiṭṭhati.

After that, in the body, one determines that pus, by way of color, has the color of a pale withered leaf. By way of shape, its shape is that of its location. By way of direction, it is produced in the two directions. By way of location, for pus there is no fixed location. Wherever in a region of the body that has been struck by such things as stumps, thorns, blows, or flames of fire, the blood collects and putrefies, or wherever boils, pimples, and so on arise, there it is situated.

Tattha yathā rukkhassa tattha tattha pharasudhārādīhi pahatappadese avagaḷitvā ṭhito niyyāso na jānāti “ahaṃ rukkhassa pahatappadese ṭhito”ti, napi rukkhassa pahatappadeso jānāti “mayi niyyāso ṭhito”ti; evameva na pubbo jānāti “ahaṃ sarīrassa tattha tattha khāṇukaṇṭakādīhi abhihatappadese gaṇḍapiḷakādīnaṃ uṭṭhitappadese vā ṭhito”ti, napi sarīrappadeso jānāti “mayi pubbo ṭhito”ti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā [M 0.0050] hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato pubbo pubbabhāgena paricchinnoti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ pubbaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as the sap of a tree, having oozed out and settled in places struck here and there by an axe, blade, and so on, does not know, “I am settled in a place of the tree that has been struck,” nor does the struck place of the tree know, “Sap is settled in me”; in this same way, pus does not know, “I am settled in this or that place of the body struck by a stump, thorn, and so on, or in a place where boils, blisters, and so on have arisen,” nor does the part of the body know, “Pus is settled in me.” For these phenomena are devoid of attending and reflecting… not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines: “Pus is delimited by the part of pus.” This is its delimitation by similar nature; its delimitation by dissimilar nature, however, is just like that of hair. Thus one determines pus by way of color and so on.

Tato paraṃ sarīre sannicitalohitaṃ saṃsaraṇalohitanti evaṃ duvidhe lohite sannicitalohitaṃ tāva vaṇṇato bahalakuthitalākhārasavaṇṇanti [P 0.0063] vavatthapeti, saṃsaraṇalohitaṃ acchalākhārasavaṇṇanti. Saṇṭhānato sabbampi attano okāsasaṇṭhānaṃ. Disato sannicitalohitaṃ uparimāya disāya jātaṃ, saṃsaraṇalohitaṃ dvīsupīti. Okāsato saṃsaraṇalohitaṃ kesalomanakhadantānaṃ maṃsavinimuttaṭṭhānañceva thaddhasukkhacammañca vajjetvā dhamanijālānusārena [V 0.0048] sabbaṃ upādinnakasarīraṃ pharitvā ṭhitaṃ. Sannicitalohitaṃ yakanassa heṭṭhābhāgaṃ pūretvā ekapattapūraṇamattaṃ vakkahadayapapphāsānaṃ upari thokaṃ thokaṃ binduṃ pātentaṃ vakkahadayayakanapapphāse tementaṃ ṭhitaṃ, yamhi vakkahadayādīni atemente sattā pipāsitā honti.

Next, in the body, of the two kinds of blood—namely, collected blood and circulating blood—one first determines collected blood by way of color as having the color of thick, boiled lac juice, and circulating blood as having the color of clear lac juice. By way of shape, all of it has the shape of its own location. By way of direction, collected blood is produced in the upper direction; circulating blood is produced in both directions. By way of location, circulating blood, avoiding the hair of the head, hair of the body, nails, and teeth, as well as places free from flesh and stiff, dry skin, stands pervading the entire appropriated body by following the network of vessels. Collected blood, filling the lower part of the liver to the measure of about one leaf-cup, stands moistening the kidneys, heart, liver, and lungs, causing drops to fall little by little upon the kidneys, heart, and lungs. When it does not moisten the kidneys, heart, and so on, beings become thirsty.

Tattha yathā jajjarakapāle ṭhitaṃ udakaṃ heṭṭhā leḍḍukhaṇḍādīni tementaṃ na jānāti “ahaṃ jajjarakapāle ṭhitaṃ heṭṭhā leḍḍukhaṇḍādīni tememī”ti, napi jajjarakapālaṃ heṭṭhā leḍḍukhaṇḍādīni vā jānanti “mayi udakaṃ ṭhitaṃ, amhe vā tementaṃ ṭhita”nti; evameva na lohitaṃ jānāti “ahaṃ yakanassa heṭṭhābhāge vakkahadayādīni tementaṃ ṭhita”nti, napi yakanassa heṭṭhābhāgaṭṭhānaṃ vakkahadayādīni vā jānanti “mayi lohitaṃ ṭhitaṃ, amhe vā tementaṃ ṭhita”nti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato lohitaṃ lohitabhāgena paricchinnanti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ lohitaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as water standing in a cracked potsherd, while moistening the clods of earth and so on below, does not know, “I, standing in a cracked potsherd, moisten the clods of earth and so on below,” nor do the cracked potsherd or the clods of earth and so on below know, “Water is standing in us, or stands moistening us”; in this same way, blood does not know, “I stand in the lower part of the liver, moistening the kidneys, heart, and so on,” nor do the place of the lower part of the liver or the kidneys, heart, and so on know, “Blood is standing in us, or stands moistening us.” For these phenomena are devoid of attending and reflecting… not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines: “Blood is delimited by the part of blood.” This is its delimitation by similar nature; its delimitation by dissimilar nature, however, is just like that of hair. Thus one determines blood by way of color and so on.

Tato paraṃ sarīre sedo vaṇṇato pasannatilatelavaṇṇoti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato okāsasaṇṭhāno. Disato dvīsu disāsu jāto. Okāsato sedassa okāso nāma nibaddho natthi, yattha sedo lohitaṃ viya sadā tiṭṭheyya. Yasmā vā yadā aggisantāpasūriyasantāpautuvikārādīhi [M 0.0051] sarīraṃ santapati, atha udakato abbūḷhamattavisamacchinnabhisamuḷālakumudanālakalāpaudakamiva sabbakesalomakūpavivarehi paggharati. Tasmā tesaṃ kesalomakūpavivarānaṃ vasena taṃ [P 0.0064] saṇṭhānato vavatthapeti. “Sedapariggaṇhakena ca yogāvacarena kesalomakūpavivare pūretvā ṭhitavaseneva sedo manasikātabbo”ti vuttaṃ pubbācariyehi.

Next, in the body, one determines sweat by way of color as having the color of clear sesame oil. By way of shape, it has the shape of its location. By way of direction, it is produced in two directions. By way of location, there is no fixed location for sweat where it might always stand, like blood. For when the body is heated by the heat of fire, the heat of the sun, changes in season, and so on, then it oozes from all the openings of the hair and body-hair pores, like water from a freshly and unevenly cut lotus root, lotus stalk, water lily stalk, or bundle of lotuses. Therefore, one determines its shape in accordance with those openings of the hair and body-hair pores. And it has been said by the ancient teachers: “Sweat should be attended to by the yogi who is comprehending sweat only as it fills and stands in the openings of the hair and body-hair pores.”

Tattha yathā bhisamuḷālakumudanālakalāpavivarehi paggharantaṃ udakaṃ na jānāti “ahaṃ bhisamuḷālakumudanālakalāpavivarehi paggharāmī”ti, napi bhisamuḷālakumudanālakalāpavivarā jānanti “amhehi udakaṃ paggharatī”ti; evameva na sedo jānāti “ahaṃ kesalomakūpavivarehi paggharāmī”ti, napi kesalomakūpavivarā jānanti “amhehi sedo paggharatī”ti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato sedo sedabhāgena paricchinnoti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ sedaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as water oozing from the openings of lotus roots, lotus stalks, water lily stalks, and bundles of lotuses does not know, “I ooze from the openings of lotus roots, lotus stalks, water lily stalks, and bundles of lotuses,” nor do the openings of the lotus roots, lotus stalks, water lily stalks, and bundles of lotuses know, “Water oozes from us”; in this same way, sweat does not know, “I ooze from the openings of the hair and body-hair pores,” nor do the openings of the hair and body-hair pores know, “Sweat oozes from us.” For these phenomena are devoid of attending and reflecting… not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines: “Sweat is delimited by the part of sweat.” This is its delimitation by similar nature; its delimitation by dissimilar nature, however, is just like that of hair. Thus one determines sweat by way of color and so on.

Tato [V 0.0049] paraṃ sarīre cammamaṃsantare medo vaṇṇato phālitahaliddivaṇṇoti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato okāsasaṇṭhāno. Tathā hi sukhino thūlasarīrassa cammamaṃsantare pharitvā ṭhito haliddirattadukūlapilotikasaṇṭhāno, kisasarīrassa jaṅghamaṃsaūrumaṃsapiṭṭhikaṇṭakanissitapiṭṭhimaṃsaudarapaṭalamaṃsāni nissāya saṃvellitvā ṭhapitahaliddirattadukūlapilotikakhaṇḍasaṇṭhāno. Disato dvīsu disāsu jāto. Okāsato thūlasarīrassa sakalasarīraṃ pharitvā kisassa jaṅghāmaṃsādīni nissāya ṭhito, yo sinehasaṅkhātopi hutvā paramajegucchattā na matthakatelatthaṃ na gaṇḍūsatelatthaṃ na dīpajālanatthaṃ saṅgayhati.

Next, in the body, one determines the solid fat between the skin and the flesh by way of color as having the color of split turmeric. By way of shape, it has the shape of its location. For in the body of a comfortable, stout person, it stands pervading the space between the skin and the flesh, having the shape of a turmeric-dyed, worn-out fine cloth. In the body of a lean person, it relies on the calf-flesh, thigh-flesh, back-flesh attached to the spine, and the flesh of the abdominal wall, and is wrinkled, having the shape of a piece of a placed, turmeric-dyed, worn-out fine cloth. By way of direction, it is produced in two directions. By way of location, in a stout person’s body it stands pervading the entire body; in a lean person’s body it stands relying on the calf-flesh and so on. Although it is also designated as ‘grease,’ because of its extreme repulsiveness it is not collected for the purpose of head-oil, for the purpose of oil for boils, or for the purpose of lighting a lamp.

Tattha yathā maṃsapuñjaṃ nissāya ṭhitā haliddirattadukūlapilotikā na jānāti “ahaṃ maṃsapuñjaṃ nissāya ṭhitā”ti, napi maṃsapuñjo jānāti “haliddirattadukūlapilotikā maṃ nissāya ṭhitā”ti; evameva na medo jānāti “ahaṃ sakalasarīraṃ jaṅghādīsu vā maṃsaṃ nissāya ṭhito”ti, napi sakalasarīraṃ jānāti jaṅghādīsu vā maṃsaṃ “medo maṃ nissāya ṭhito”ti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato medo heṭṭhā maṃsena, upari cammena, samantato medabhāgena [M 0.0052] paricchinnoti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo [P 0.0065] pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ medaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as a worn-out fine cloth dyed with turmeric, resting on a lump of flesh, does not know, 'I am resting on a lump of flesh,' nor does the lump of flesh know, 'A worn-out fine cloth dyed with turmeric is resting on me'; even so, the solid fat does not know, 'I am resting on the entire body or on the flesh in the shanks and other parts,' nor does the entire body or the flesh in the shanks and other parts know, 'The solid fat is resting on me.' For these phenomena are devoid of adverting and reviewing... (etc.)... they are not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines that the solid fat is delimited below by flesh, above by skin, and all around by the portion of solid fat. This is its homogeneous delimitation; its heterogeneous delimitation, however, is just like that of the hair. Thus one determines the solid fat by way of its color and so forth.

Tato paraṃ sarīre assu vaṇṇato pasannatilatelavaṇṇanti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato okāsasaṇṭhānaṃ. Disato uparimāya disāya jātaṃ. Okāsato akkhikūpakesu ṭhitanti. Na cetaṃ pittakosake pittamiva akkhikūpakesu sadā sannicitaṃ hutvā tiṭṭhati, kintu yadā somanassajātā sattā mahāhasitaṃ hasanti, domanassajātā rodanti paridevanti, tathārūpaṃ visamāhāraṃ vā haranti, yadā ca tesaṃ akkhīni dhūmarajapaṃsukādīhi abhihaññanti, tadā etehi somanassadomanassavisamāhārādīhi samuṭṭhahitvā assu akkhikūpakesu pūretvā tiṭṭhati paggharati ca. “Assupariggaṇhakena ca yogāvacarena akkhikūpake pūretvā ṭhitavaseneva taṃ manasikātabba”nti pubbācariyā vaṇṇayanti.

Thereafter, regarding the tears in the body, one determines: by color, they have the color of clear sesame oil. By shape, they have the shape of their location. By direction, they arise in the upper direction. By location, they are situated in the eye sockets. And they do not always remain, having accumulated in the eye sockets, like bile in the gallbladder. But rather, when beings who have become joyful laugh a great laugh, or those who have become sorrowful weep and lament, or consume unsuitable food of that kind, and when their eyes are afflicted by smoke, dust, dirt, and so on, then, arising from such joy, sorrow, unsuitable food, and so on, tears, having filled the eye sockets, remain and also flow out. The ancient teachers explain: 'And by the yogi who comprehends tears, they should be attended to solely by way of their remaining after having filled the eye sockets.'

Tattha yathā matthakacchinnataruṇatālaṭṭhikūpakesu ṭhitaṃ udakaṃ na jānāti “ahaṃ matthakacchinnataruṇatālaṭṭhikūpakesu ṭhita”nti, napi matthakacchinnataruṇatālaṭṭhikūpakā jānanti “amhesu udakaṃ ṭhita”nti; evameva na assu jānāti “ahaṃ akkhikūpakesu ṭhita”nti, napi akkhikūpakā jānanti “amhesu assu ṭhita”nti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete [V 0.0050] dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato assu assubhāgena paricchinnanti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ assuṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as water situated in the cavities of young palm seeds with their stalks cut off does not know, 'I am situated in the cavities of young palm seeds with their stalks cut off,' nor do the cavities of young palm seeds with their stalks cut off know, 'Water is situated in us'; even so, tears do not know, 'I am situated in the eye sockets,' nor do the eye sockets know, 'Tears are situated in us.' For these phenomena are devoid of adverting and reviewing... (etc.)... they are not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines that tears are delimited by the portion of tears. This is their homogeneous delimitation; their heterogeneous delimitation, however, is just like that of the hair. Thus one determines tears by way of their color and so forth.

Tato paraṃ sarīre vilīnasinehasaṅkhātā vasā vaṇṇato ācāme āsittatelavaṇṇāti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato okāsasaṇṭhānā. Disato dvīsu disāsu jātā. Okāsato hatthatalahatthapiṭṭhipādatalapādapiṭṭhināsāpuṭanalāṭaaṃsakūṭesu ṭhitāti. Na cesā etesu okāsesu sadā vilīnā eva hutvā tiṭṭhati, kintu yadā aggisantāpasūriyasantāpautuvisabhāgadhātuvisabhāgehi te padesā usmājātā honti, tadā tattha vilīnāva hutvā pasannasalilāsu udakasoṇḍikāsu nīhāro viya sarati.

Thereafter, regarding the liquid fat in the body, known as dissolved grease, one determines: by color, it has the color of oil poured on rice scum. By shape, it has the shape of its location. By direction, it arises in two directions. By location, it is situated in the palms of the hands, the backs of the hands, the soles of the feet, the backs of the feet, the bridge of the nose, the forehead, and the tips of the shoulders. And this does not always remain in these locations, having become dissolved. But rather, when those areas become heated due to the heat of fire, the heat of the sun, imbalance of season, or imbalance of elements, then, having become dissolved there, it flows like vapor over the clear water in lime-washed tanks.

Tattha [M 0.0053] yathā udakasoṇḍiyo ajjhottharitvā [P 0.0066] ṭhito nīhāro na jānāti “ahaṃ udakasoṇḍiyo ajjhottharitvā ṭhito”ti, napi udakasoṇḍiyo jānanti “nīhāro amhe ajjhottharitvā ṭhito”ti; evameva na vasā jānāti “ahaṃ hatthatalādīni ajjhottharitvā ṭhitā”ti, napi hatthatalādīni jānanti “vasā amhe ajjhottharitvā ṭhitā”ti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato vasā vasābhāgena paricchinnāti vavatthapeti. Ayametissā sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ vasaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as vapor that, having overspread lime-washed tanks, is situated there does not know, 'I, having overspread lime-washed tanks, am situated there,' nor do the lime-washed tanks know, 'Vapor, having overspread us, is situated there'; even so, the liquid fat does not know, 'I, having overspread the palms of the hands and other parts, am situated there,' nor do the palms of the hands and other parts know, 'Liquid fat, having overspread us, is situated there.' For these phenomena are devoid of adverting and reviewing... (etc.)... they are not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines that liquid fat is delimited by the portion of liquid fat. This is its homogeneous delimitation; its heterogeneous delimitation, however, is just like that of the hair. Thus one determines liquid fat by way of its color and so forth.

Tato paraṃ sarīre mukhassabbhantare kheḷo vaṇṇato seto pheṇavaṇṇoti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato okāsasaṇṭhānoti, samuddapheṇasaṇṭhānotipi eke. Disato uparimāya disāya jāto. Okāsato ubhohi kapolapassehi orohitvā jivhāya ṭhitoti. Na ceso ettha sadā sannicito hutvā tiṭṭhati, kintu yadā sattā tathārūpaṃ āhāraṃ passanti vā saranti vā, uṇhatittakaṭukaloṇambilānaṃ vā kiñci mukhe ṭhapenti. Yadā ca tesaṃ hadayaṃ āgilāyati, kismiñcideva vā jigucchā uppajjati, tadā kheḷo uppajjitvā ubhohi kapolapassehi orohitvā jivhāya saṇṭhāti. Aggajivhāya cesa kheḷo tanuko hoti, mūlajivhāya bahalo, mukhe pakkhittañca puthukaṃ vā taṇḍulaṃ vā aññaṃ vā kiñci khādanīyaṃ nadipuline khatakūpasalilamiva parikkhayamagacchantova sadā temanasamattho hoti.

Thereafter, regarding the saliva within the mouth in the body, one determines: by color, it is white, with the color of foam. By shape, it has the shape of its location; some say it has the shape of sea-foam. By direction, it arises in the upper direction. By location, having descended from both cheeks, it is situated on the tongue. And this does not always remain there, having accumulated. But rather, when beings see or recollect such food, or place something hot, bitter, pungent, salty, or sour in the mouth; and when their heart is afflicted, or disgust arises for some reason whatsoever, then saliva, having arisen, descends from both cheeks and settles on the tongue. And this saliva is thin at the tip of the tongue and thick at the root of the tongue. It is always able to moisten flattened rice, or uncooked rice, or any other kind of edible food placed in the mouth, just like the water in a well dug by hand on a river's sandbank, which does not go to exhaustion.

Tattha yathā nadipuline khatakūpatale saṇṭhitaṃ udakaṃ na jānāti “ahaṃ kūpatale saṇṭhita”nti[V 0.0051], napi kūpatalaṃ jānāti “mayi udakaṃ ṭhita”nti; evameva na kheḷo jānāti “ahaṃ ubhohi kapolapassehi orohitvā jivhātale saṇṭhito”ti, napi jivhātalaṃ jānāti “mayi ubhohi kapolapassehi orohitvā kheḷo saṇṭhito”ti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato kheḷo kheḷabhāgena paricchinnoti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ kheḷaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as water resting in a dug pit on a riverbank does not know, 'I am resting in a dug pit,' nor does the dug pit know, 'Water is resting in me'; even so, saliva does not know, 'Having descended from both cheeks, I am resting on the surface of the tongue,' nor does the surface of the tongue know, 'Having descended from both cheeks, saliva is resting on me.' For these phenomena are devoid of advertence and reflection... not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines: 'Saliva is delimited by the part that is saliva.' This is its homogeneous delimitation; its heterogeneous delimitation, however, is just like the hair. In this way, one determines saliva by way of color and so forth.

Tato [M 0.0054][P 0.0067] paraṃ sarīre siṅghāṇikā vaṇṇato setā taruṇatālamiñjavaṇṇāti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato okāsasaṇṭhānā, sedetvā sedetvā nāsāpuṭe nirantaraṃ pakkhittavettaṅkurasaṇṭhānātipi eke. Disato uparimāya disāya jātā. Okāsato nāsāpuṭe pūretvā ṭhitāti. Na cesā ettha sadā sannicitā hutvā tiṭṭhati, kintu seyyathāpi nāma puriso paduminipatte dadhiṃ bandhitvā heṭṭhā paduminipattaṃ kaṇṭakena vijjheyya, atha tena chiddena dadhipiṇḍaṃ gaḷitvā bahi papateyya; evameva yadā sattā rodanti, visabhāgāhārautuvasena vā sañjātadhātukkhobhā honti, tadā antosīsato pūtisemhabhāvaṃ āpannaṃ matthaluṅgaṃ gaḷitvā tālumatthakavivarena otaritvā nāsāpuṭe pūretvā tiṭṭhati.

Then, further, in the body, one determines that nasal mucus is white in color, like the color of a young palm kernel. In terms of shape, it has the shape of the space it occupies; some say its shape is like a rattan shoot continuously inserted into the nostrils from repeated dripping. In terms of direction, it arises from the upper direction. In terms of location, it fills the nostrils and remains. But it does not always remain accumulated there; rather, just as a man might wrap curds in a lotus leaf and pierce the lotus leaf underneath with a thorn, and then the lump of curds would ooze through that hole and fall outside; even so, when beings cry, or when disturbances of the elements arise due to unsuitable food or seasonal changes, the brain, having become a putrid and phlegm-like substance, oozes down through the opening at the top of the palate and remains, filling the nostrils.

Tattha yathā sippikāya pakkhittaṃ pūtidadhi na jānāti “ahaṃ sippikāya ṭhita”nti, napi sippikā jānāti “mayi pūtikaṃ dadhi ṭhita”nti; evameva na siṅghāṇikā jānāti “ahaṃ nāsāpuṭesu ṭhitā”ti, napi nāsāpuṭā jānanti “amhesu siṅghāṇikā ṭhitā”ti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato siṅghāṇikā siṅghāṇikabhāgena paricchinnāti vavatthapeti. Ayametissā sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ siṅghāṇikaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as putrid curds placed in an oyster shell do not know, 'I am placed in an oyster shell,' nor does the oyster shell know, 'Putrid curds are placed in me'; even so, nasal mucus does not know, 'I am situated in the nostrils,' nor do the nostrils know, 'Nasal mucus is situated in us.' For these phenomena are devoid of advertence and reflection... not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines: 'Nasal mucus is delimited by the part that is nasal mucus.' This is its homogeneous delimitation; its heterogeneous delimitation, however, is just like the hair. In this way, one determines nasal mucus by way of color and so forth.

Tato paraṃ antosarīre lasikāti sarīrasandhīnaṃ abbhantare picchilakuṇapaṃ. Sā vaṇṇato kaṇikāraniyyāsavaṇṇāti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato okāsasaṇṭhānā. Disato dvīsu disāsu jātā. Okāsato aṭṭhisandhīnaṃ abbhañjanakiccaṃ sādhayamānā asītisatasandhīnaṃ abbhantare ṭhitāti. Yassa cesā mandā hoti, tassa uṭṭhahantassa nisīdantassa abhikkamantassa paṭikkamantassa samiñjantassa pasārentassa aṭṭhikāni kaṭakaṭāyanti, accharikāsaddaṃ karonto viya vicarati[P 0.0068], ekayojanadviyojanamattampi addhānaṃ gatassa vāyodhātu kuppati, gattāni dukkhanti [V 0.0052] yassa pana cesā bahukā hoti, tassa uṭṭhānanisajjādīsu na aṭṭhīni kaṭakaṭāyanti, dīghampi addhānaṃ gatassa na vāyodhātu kuppati, na gattāni dukkhanti.

Then, further inside the body, there is synovial fluid—a slimy, repulsive substance within the joints of the body. One determines that in terms of color, it has the color resembling the resin of the kaṇikāra tree. In terms of shape, it has the shape of the space it occupies. In terms of direction, it arises in two directions. In terms of location, performing the function of lubricating the bone joints, it is situated inside the one hundred and eighty joints. For one in whom this fluid is deficient, when they stand up, sit down, walk forward, walk backward, bend, or stretch, their bones creak, moving about as if making the sound of a finger-snap. Even after traveling a distance of one or two yojanas, the wind element becomes disturbed, and their limbs ache. But for one in whom this fluid is abundant, when they stand up, sit down, and so on, their bones do not creak. Even after traveling a long distance, the wind element does not become disturbed, nor do their limbs ache.

Tattha [M 0.0055] yathā abbhañjanatelaṃ na jānāti “ahaṃ akkhaṃ abbhañjitvā ṭhita”nti, napi akkho jānāti “maṃ telaṃ abbhañjitvā ṭhita”nti; evameva na lasikā jānāti “ahaṃ asītisatasandhiyo abbhañjitvā ṭhitā”ti, napi asītisatasandhiyo jānanti “lasikā amhe abbhañjitvā ṭhitā”ti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato lasikā lasikabhāgena paricchinnāti vavatthapeti. Ayametissā sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ lasikaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Therein, just as lubricating oil does not know, 'I am situated, having lubricated the axle,' nor does the axle know, 'The oil is situated, having lubricated me'; even so, the synovial fluid does not know, 'I am situated, having lubricated the one hundred and eighty joints,' nor do the one hundred and eighty joints know, 'The synovial fluid is situated, having lubricated us.' For these phenomena are devoid of advertence and reflection... not a person. By way of delimitation, one determines: 'The synovial fluid is delimited by the part that is synovial fluid.' This is its homogeneous delimitation; its heterogeneous delimitation, however, is just like the hair. In this way, one determines the synovial fluid by way of color and so forth.

Tato paraṃ antosarīre muttaṃ vaṇṇato māsakhārodakavaṇṇanti vavatthapeti. Saṇṭhānato udakaṃ pūretvā adhomukhaṭhapitaudakakumbhaantaragataudakasaṇṭhānaṃ. Disato heṭṭhimāya disāya jātaṃ. Okāsato vatthissabbhantare ṭhitanti. Vatthi nāma vatthipuṭo vuccati, yattha seyyathāpi nāma candanikāya pakkhitte amukhe peḷāghaṭe candanikāraso pavisati, na cassa pavisanamaggo paññāyati; evameva sarīrato muttaṃ pavisati, na cassa pavisanamaggo paññāyati nikkhamanamaggo eva tu pākaṭo hoti, yamhi ca muttassa bharite “passāvaṃ karomā”ti sattānaṃ āyūhanaṃ hoti. Tattha yathā candanikāya pakkhitte amukhe peḷāghaṭe ṭhito candanikāraso na jānāti “ahaṃ amukhe peḷāghaṭe ṭhito”ti, napi peḷāghaṭo jānāti “mayi candanikāraso ṭhito”ti; evameva muttaṃ na jānāti “ahaṃ vatthimhi ṭhita”nti, napi vatthi jānāti “mayi muttaṃ ṭhita”nti. Ābhogapaccavekkhaṇavirahitā hi ete dhammā…pe… na puggaloti. Paricchedato vatthiabbhantarena ceva muttabhāgena ca paricchinnanti vavatthapeti. Ayametassa [P 0.0069] sabhāgaparicchedo, visabhāgaparicchedo pana kesasadiso evāti evaṃ muttaṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti. Evamayaṃ imaṃ dvattiṃsākāraṃ vaṇṇādito vavatthapeti.

Then, further inside the body, one determines that urine, by way of color, has the color of bean broth or lye-water. By way of shape, it has the shape of water contained within a water pot that has been filled and placed upside down. By way of direction, it arises from the lower direction. By way of location, it is situated within the bladder. The bladder is called the bladder-pouch. For instance, just as when a sealed earthen pot is placed in a cesspool, the cesspool water seeps in, but its entry path is not discerned; just so, urine enters from the body, but its entry path is not discerned; only its exit path is evident.
